sermōcĭnātrix , īcis, f. sermocinator,
I.that converses, adapted to conversation; in rhet. lang., as a part of rhetoric, a transl. of the Platonic προσομιλητική, Quint. 3, 4, 10.—In gen.: “immodica,” i. e. a prattler, babbler, App. M. 9, p. 224, 31 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
